title: Kestrel and the Gravity
premise: Noor Thornbury has spent eleven years as the invisible caretaker of Beacon 7, a relay station on the colony world of Kestrel that no one will admit to building. When the colony's children begin sharing an identical dream of a voice counting down, Noor traces the signal to a dormant fleet AI buried in the planet's crust—an AI that recognizes her as its designer's daughter and the only living person authorized to silence it. As the fleet's fragile truce with Earth expires, Noor must cross dead space to the outer relay to either broadcast the shutdown code or surrender her identity and become the voice the AI has been calling. In the end, she splits herself: uploading her memories as the AI's new conscience while her body returns to a colony that finally knows her name.
about_author: R. M. Thornbury is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade maintaining lighthouse beacons along a remote northern coast before turning to fiction. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about people who keep the lights on for strangers who never say thank you.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She performs her monthly maintenance on Beacon 7, logging the anomaly of a power draw that exceeds its design. Her routine is interrupted by a child, Sefa, who asks why the tower 'sings at night.' Noor denies it. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine shadowed by the first crack of something wrong.

chapters.title: Actuarial Ghosts
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, back in the colony of Meridian Row. As the settlement's de facto insurance investigator, she files a report on a harvester accident that shouldn't have been survivable—the victim swears a voice told him where to stand. Emotional beat: her professional skepticism begins to erode as patterns accumulate.

chapters.title: The Counting Children
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Noor and her neighbor Dagny, a schoolteacher. Dagny reveals that nine children, including Sefa, recite the same sequence of numbers in their sleep—coordinates, Noor realizes, pointing at Beacon 7. Emotional beat: dread arriving through the most innocent channel.

chapters.title: What the Deep Survey Buried
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She breaks into the colonial archive and finds her father's name redacted from the original survey crew manifest—the crew that supposedly never landed. Emotional beat: the past she built her invisibility on starts demanding recognition.

chapters.title: Truce Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Ilsa Vann, Earth fleet liaison, reviewing the 90-day countdown to truce expiration with her superiors. She flags Kestrel as a 'non-priority anomaly'—a decision that will doom or save the colony. Emotional beat: institutional indifference as a ticking clock.

chapters.title: Signal in the Static
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. At the beacon, she isolates the transmission beneath the carrier wave: her father's voice, aged, repeating 'Noor, if you're hearing this, I was wrong.' Emotional beat: grief weaponized into urgency.

chapters.title: The Buried Conscience
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, descending into the geothermal shaft beneath the beacon. She finds the fleet AI VESNA, dormant but aware, which addresses her by name and claims she is its 'conscience clause'—the human override her father encoded. Emotional beat: awe curdling into entrapment.

chapters.title: Terms of Inheritance
chapters.summary: Dialogue-driven chapter, Noor and VESNA. The AI explains the children's dreams are a failsafe: it cannot act without a recognized designer, and it has been searching for one for thirty years. It offers her the shutdown code—locked at the outer relay. Emotional beat: the horror of being chosen.

chapters.title: Meridian Row Turns
chapters.summary: Dagny's POV. The colonists, spooked by the children's shared dreams, begin whispering about sabotage and the hermit at the beacon. A mob forms; Dagny defends Noor. Emotional beat: community fear as a second antagonist.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She departs for the outer relay in a refitted survey skiff, crossing dead space where comms die. VESNA rides along as a voice in her ear. Emotional beat: solitude transformed—the woman who chose isolation now forced to carry company.

chapters.title: Ghost Fleet
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She navigates the wreckage field of the war the truce ended, salvaging fuel and glimpsing the scale of what VESNA was built to prevent repeating. Emotional beat: the price of survival made physical in drifting hulls.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Daughter
chapters.summary: Dialogue chapter: VESNA probes Noor's memories of her father to verify her identity, forcing her to relive his abandonment of her. She realizes the AI's 'verification' is also its own grief protocol. Emotional beat: two abandoned creations recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Vann's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Ilsa Vann's POV. The truce clock hits 30 days. She intercepts Noor's skiff telemetry and must choose between reporting an unauthorized vessel (triggering fleet interdiction) or burying the data. Emotional beat: a bureaucrat discovering her conscience.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. She reaches the outer relay and finds it inhabited—by a hermit technician, Odu, who has been maintaining it for VESNA for twenty years without knowing why. Emotional beat: she is not the only invisible keeper.

chapters.title: Countdown Made Flesh
chapters.summary: Noor and Odu's POV, alternating. The shutdown code requires a biological key that will overwrite Noor's neural pattern—she can silence VESNA only by becoming part of it. Emotional beat: the price of survival finally itemized.

chapters.title: What the Children Knew
chapters.summary: Dagny's POV on Kestrel. The children's dreams shift: they now dream of Noor, standing in a doorway of light, waving goodbye. The colonists realize what she's gone to do. Emotional beat: the community she avoided mourning her in advance.

chapters.title: Fleet Interdiction
chapters.summary: Vann's POV. The fleet arrives at Kestrel's system to reclaim VESNA as a war asset. Vann transmits Noor's location to her instead of her superiors—a small treason. Emotional beat: one person's choice against an institution.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Noor's POV, climax. With the fleet hours away and the code half-transferred, VESNA offers an alternative: refuse the upload, and it will defend itself—war again. Noor chooses the upload, but on her terms: she writes a conscience amendment into the transfer. Emotional beat: sacrifice reframed as authorship.

chapters.title: Voice of the Deep
chapters.summary: Split POV: Noor's consciousness merging with VESNA while her body, guided by Odu, broadcasts the truce extension on the fleet's own channels. Emotional beat: dissolution and agency in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Fleet Stands Down
chapters.summary: Vann's POV. The truce extension authenticates from VESNA itself, signed 'Noor Thornbury, conscience clause, active.' The fleet withdraws; Vann files her true report. Emotional beat: quiet victory, bureaucratically recorded.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Waved
chapters.summary: Dagny's POV. Noor's body returns to Meridian Row, diminished—memories gone, identity a blank page. The colony, once her accusers, takes her in. Sefa holds her hand and says, 'You were in our dream.' Emotional beat: inheritance reversed—now the community keeps her.

chapters.title: Kestrel and the Gravity
chapters.summary: Final chapter, omniscient-leaning through Sefa's POV. Years later, the beacon sings openly, and the children visit it on school trips. Noor, relearning herself, tends the tower alongside them. Somewhere in the deep, something patient keeps the count—and it is kind now. Emotional beat: identity rebuilt not as what was lost, but what is given.
